title: An element of a module vanishing in the localizations at a spanning family is zero
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $s\subseteq R$ a subset generating the unit ideal, and $M$ an $R$-module. If $m\in M$ satisfies $m/1=0$ in $M_f$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] for every $f\in s$, then $m=0$.

source.place: Lemma 00EO (label lemma-cover) (1), applied to the submodule $Rm\subseteq M$ (whose localizations $(Rm)_{f}\subseteq M_f$ are generated by $m/1$)

mathlib_searches.query: if x in M maps to zero in the localization M_r for every r in a set spanning the unit ideal, then x = 0
element of a module that becomes zero in the localizations at each element of a family generating the unit ideal is zero

mathlib_searches.results: Module.eq_of_isLocalized_span (Submodule.lean:153), Module.eq_zero_of_isLocalized_span (:161): for `Ideal.span s = ⊤`, localizations `f r : M →ₗ[R] Mₚ r` with `IsLocalizedModule.Away r.1 (f r)` (and Rₚ r with IsLocalization.Away), `x : M`, `∀ r : s, f r x = 0 → x = 0`

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: take `Rₚ r = Localization.Away r.1`, `Mₚ r = LocalizedModule.Away r.1 M`, `f r = LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap _ M`
